title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper analyzes the resilience of the euro-denominated repo market during episodes of financial stress using transaction-level data and network analysis. The institutional repo network exhibits a core-periphery structure, with connectivity intensifying during stress periods. Key finding: at the market level, borrowing costs decline as financial stress increases, indicating the euro repo market functions as a shock absorber rather than a transmission vector for stress.
key_points: The euro repo market is the largest segment of the euro money market, accounting for 56% of daily transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts
The repo market exhibits a core-periphery structure with a small core of highly active institutions doing most of the trading
Network connectivity between institutions, especially bank-to-bank trading, has grown over time even during stress periods
Trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable at the sectoral level under stress
At the market level, borrowing costs decline as financial stress increases—the market acts as a shock absorber
The analysis covers euro-denominated repo transactions from 2021 to mid-February 2025 using SFTDS transaction-level data
why_it_matters: Repo markets are essential channels for liquidity circulation in the financial system. This research provides empirical evidence on how the euro repo market maintains resilience during stress episodes, which has direct implications for financial stability monitoring and repo market regulation. Understanding the network structure helps identify which links are critical and how stress propagates through the system.
market_structure_context: The paper provides detailed analysis of repo market network topology (core-periphery structure), connectivity dynamics under stress, and sector-level trading patterns. It examines network density and strength metrics alongside repo market variables including trading volumes, spreads, haircuts, and maturities. The institutional network maps repo activity between counterparties, while the sectoral network tracks aggregate patterns.
important_numbers: 56% of daily euro money market transactions
30% of outstanding amounts in euro money market
4.9% increase in total outstanding repos from June 2023 to June 2024
notes: High-quality ECB working paper using transaction-level SFTDS data. Source explicitly addresses market structure through network analysis methodology. Published via ECB Working Paper Series (No 3205). The research is empirically grounded with 2021-2025 data and uses CISS for financial stress measurement. No market reaction or price action predictions inferred. Market impact confidence set to 0 as this is academic research without explicit market direction signals.
